free_tier.stated: RMB 30.00/month for hk.st.s on the Hong Kong large-disk line: 1 vCPU Xeon Gold, 1 GiB RAM, 250 GiB SSD, 1,000 Mbps port, 5,000 GB/month traffic, one IPv4 on the international-native route; annual billing RMB 300.00. The ladder above it is hk.st.m at RMB 55.00/month (2 vCPU, 2 GiB, 500 GiB, 2,000 Mbps, 10,000 GB/month, annual RMB 550.00), hk.st.l at RMB 100.00/month (4 vCPU, 4 GiB, 1,000 GiB, 3,500 Mbps, 20,000 GB/month, annual RMB 1,000.00) and hk.st.xl at RMB 180.00/month (8 vCPU, 8 GiB, 2,000 GiB, 5,000 Mbps, 40,000 GB/month, annual RMB 1,800.00). The cheapest classic plan of any kind on the same table is hk.cld.s at RMB 25.00/month (1 vCPU Xeon E5, 1 GiB, 20 GiB, 50 Mbps, 300 GB/month, annual RMB 250.00). Elastic cloud starts at RMB 29.52/month for hardware alone: the page's own footer reads 'create your elastic cloud server from RMB 29.52/month', and the datacenter block is headed 'the prices below are each datacenter's hardware starting price'. Prices are as printed in yuan; no conversion is made anywhere in this record.

egress.terms: the four Hong Kong large-disk plans state 5,000 / 10,000 / 20,000 / 40,000 GB a month on 1,000 / 2,000 / 3,500 / 5,000 Mbps ports. No overage price and no post-allowance throttle price are printed on the plan page; the classic FAQ states that when traffic is exhausted the port speed drops to the minimum without stopping the machine, and the allowance resets next billing month. Elastic cloud meters traffic separately from the hardware price; the per-GB rate sits behind the console sign-in and was not read.
egress.free_allowance: 5,000 GB per month on hk.st.s, 10,000 GB on hk.st.m, 20,000 GB on hk.st.l, 40,000 GB on hk.st.xl; the classic line resets monthly and throttles rather than stops

interface_detail: inferred from the tooling the provider documents; not probed
tooling: the homepage links a Postman collection under 'API doc' at https://documenter.getpostman.com/view/10267761/SWTK4u2K, which was not opened. Classic plans are ordered per plan at vm.dogyun.com/server/create/<id> and elastic cloud is configured at cvm.dogyun.com/server/create, which returned a sign-in form to an unauthenticated fetch, so the configurator, its add-on prices and the per-GB traffic rate were not read. No rclone or S3-compatible interface is offered: this is a raw Linux box. That is a tooling note and not a verdict, because the resource exists and is reachable through the panel.
chaining: 250 GiB with 5 TB a month for RMB 30 is about RMB 0.12 per GiB per month, the cheapest big-disk row read, and the ladder to 2 TiB for RMB 180 still carries 40 TB a month, so the whole series is an archive tier rather than a compute tier. It fits a cold backup target, a mirror or a media archive driven over rsync or restic. The terms' ban on sustained disk I/O, on PT/BT downloads and on proxy use rules out a seedbox or a hot database index, and the terms state that the VPS line carries no data redundancy: RAID is called an availability measure, not a backup, so the client's own second copy is mandatory before treating it as 2 TiB of durable archive.

refund terms, quoted and translated: 'we only support refunds to the original payment channel; once the time limit is passed the order closes automatically and no refund is possible'; 'refunds incur a 5% channel fee'; 'the refund is self-service: destroy the product, ensure the balance is sufficient, enter the recharge order and click refund'. Resource rules: 'do not occupy a large amount of bandwidth for a long time or run software that affects network performance, including PT downloads, BT downloads, Thunder, eMule'; 'do not occupy a large amount of disk I/O for a long time or run software that affects server stability, including disk DD tests, disk scans and antivirus software'; 'do not occupy a large amount of CPU for a long time ... including CPU benchmarks, Linux benchmark scripts and video transcoding software'; 'do not use the service as a proxy (VPN or any proxy nature)'. Redundancy: 'server products do not provide data redundancy backup, please do your own off-site backup (RAID only raises disk reliability, it is not a backup); for data loss from a catastrophic failure we compensate one month of the same plan (excluding non-array products)'.
